author: elikoga
body:
PL-135522

Removing a model from inference but not the gateway makes the system 500 forever.

The update_manifest handler raises HTTPException(500) when the gateway requests models the inference server doesn't know about. FastAPI's built-in handler catches this before the custom @app.exception_handler(Exception) gets it, so the error detail was silently swallowed -- only visible in the bare status code in access.log.

Fix:
- Add log.error() in manager.py before raising the HTTPException, including the unknown, requested, and configured model lists.
- Add @app.exception_handler(HTTPException) in the inference app that logs any HTTPException with status >= 500 at ERROR level with the full detail, then returns the standard error response.

author: rickbutterfield
body:
## Problem

Deleting a workspace that still contains automations returns HTTP 409 with a ProblemDetails body explaining why ("Cannot delete a workspace that contains automations. Delete or move the automations first."). The backoffice ignored it and showed the generic **"A fatal server error occurred"** instead.

Two compounding defects caused this:

1. **Backend body missing `type`.** `DeleteWorkspaceController` built the 409 via raw `new ProblemDetails { Title, Detail, Status }`, leaving `Type = null` (omitted from JSON). The CMS API interceptor only merges a server body when `isProblemDetailsLike(body)` is true, which **requires a `type` property** — so the detail was discarded and it fell back to the default title. Every other endpoint uses `ProblemDetailsBuilder` (which defaults `Type = "Error"`), so they were unaffected.
2. **Frontend read the wrong field.** `UaDeleteActionBase` cast the error as `{ title, detail }`, but a `tryExecute` `UmbApiError` carries those under `error.problemDetails`. So even once the body survived the interceptor, the delete action couldn't read the title/detail and fell back to its generic message.

## Fix

- `DeleteWorkspaceController` builds the 409 with `ProblemDetailsBuilder` (so it carries `type`).
- The shared `ConcurrencyConflict` helper in `UmbracoAutomateManagementControllerBase` now uses `ProblemDetailsBuilder` too — same root cause, also covers workspace/connection update.
- `delete.action.ts` reads `error.problemDetails.title/detail` first (falling back to direct fields). On the 17.x target this entity action is the single notifier — plain `tryExecute` does **not** auto-notify on 17.x — so it surfaces the server's title/detail via `umbPeekError`.

## Validation

Verified end-to-end on a local 17.3.4 demo (Playwright): deleting a non-empty workspace now shows a single danger toast — **"Workspace not empty" / "Cannot delete a workspace that contains automations. Delete or move the automations first."** — and the workspace is not deleted. Network confirmed the 409 body now includes `type: "Error"`.

## Notes

- **v18 follow-up:** On Umbraco 18.x, plain `tryExecute` auto-notifies from the ProblemDetails body, which would produce a duplicate toast alongside the action's own peek. When migrating to v18, reconcile the notification strategy across all delete data sources (workspace, connection, automation) — e.g. disable the built-in notification or stop notifying from the action.
- The same `type`-less `ProblemDetails` pattern exists in `WebhookEndpointController` and the workspace-group create/update controllers, and the same frontend field-access bug exists in the bulk-delete action. Left untouched as outside this issue's scope — follow-up candidates.

## Tests

- No existing controller tests cover delete-workspace, so none to update.
- Backend (`Umbraco.Automate.Web`) builds with 0 errors; frontend `tsc --noEmit` exits 0 and `npm run build` (tsc + vite) succeeds.

Closes #74

## Summary

E3.2 **PR-C** — completes the `ISecretStore` design (SPEC-050 §3) on top of the existing per-OS backends, the last PR in the Environments epic. This is the flagged-risk item (the Linux fallback); it is now spec-faithful and CI-safe on all three OSes.

- **Interface** — add `ExistsAsync` + `Info` (`SecretStoreInfo {BackendName, IsOsKeychain, LimitationNote}`) per SPEC-050 §3.1, implemented across all five backends, the router, and `FakeSecretStore`.
- **Encrypted-file fallback (SEC-023)** — the data key is no longer persisted. It is **HKDF-SHA256-derived** per session from `machine-id ∥ uid ∥ a random per-install salt` (salt + data files `0600`); AES-256-GCM with a per-secret nonce. A fresh instance over the same directory re-derives the same key (tested), so secrets survive restart; a backend change means re-entry (SEC-025, no migration).
- **Router selection (SEC-025)** — `SecretStore` probes the native backend **once at startup** (platform → keychain probe → fallback), commits to native-or-fallback, and **logs the choice** (name only) through an injected sink. It still demotes to the fallback if the native backend fails mid-session (defence in depth).

On a tenant subdomain the middleware bounces any absolute `/org/<slug>/*` link the app emits to its prefix-stripped equivalent (`/admin`, `/login`, …), which the existing rewrite maps back to the canonical route internally. ## What

- Replace the Weixin adapter fallback `messageId` for messages without `message_id` with a deterministic hash.
- Cover iLink re-delivery of the same logical message with a regression test.

## Why

iLink can re-deliver a Weixin inbound message without `message_id`. The old fallback used `Date.now()` plus `Math.random()`, so each replay received a different `messageId` and bypassed inbound deduplication, processing the same user message twice.

The new fallback fingerprints sender, context token, create time, item type, text/media key, and filename. Re-delivery of the same logical message gets the same fallback id, while distinct context tokens remain distinct.

Addresses #925 (dedup layer only — cursor/ack root cause is a separate follow-up)

author: chadheise
body:
## Changes

### 1. \`pwm_bits: 8\` in config.yaml
Step 3 of the tuning ladder. Reduces PWM color depth from default 11 to 8, which stabilizes the PWM output and reduces artifacts on white/bright content. Slight color depth tradeoff (256 vs 2048 steps per channel), unlikely to be perceptible on LED panels.

### 2. Hardware render loop no longer sleeps after SwapOnVSync
On hardware, \`SwapOnVSync\` runs in a thread executor and blocks until the next hardware vsync (~20ms at 50 Hz). The previous \`asyncio.sleep(33ms)\` after each render compounded this, capping actual frame delivery to ~19 FPS — well below the hardware refresh rate. Removing the sleep on hardware lets the loop deliver frames as fast as the hardware can consume them (~50 FPS). Simulator mode keeps the sleep to cap at the configured FPS target.

## Test
Restart the engine and check white horizontal stripe content for artifacts. Also verify the display feels smoother overall.

body:
**Stacked on #12** (admin CLI). Fixes the "one person → multiple *unmapped* contributors" bug and adds avatars.

## Root cause
A person commits under several git identities (`john@john-ellison.com` **and** `johnellison@users.noreply.github.com`); the read grouped by git-email and there was no alias mechanism — so one person rendered as several "unmapped" rows.

## Fix
- **`member_emails`** alias table — **`unique(team_id, email)`** so an alias maps to at most one member (can't silently re-fragment). Plus `members.github_login`/`avatar_url`. (`postgres/schema.sql`; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` drift + Sources-of-truth updated in the same change.)
- **Ingest** (`buildAuthorMap`) folds aliases into `byEmail` as **exact** matches — alias domains are *not* added to the handle heuristic, preserving #11's misattribution fix.
- **Read** (`getCodebaseDetail`) groups by **`member_id ?? unmapped:<author_key>`** → one row per person, with avatar/login. Storage stays per-identity/day (no physical collapse).
- **`addAuthorAlias`** — insert alias + backfill contributions; **collision-safe** (rows mapped to another member are reported, re-pointed only with `--force`).
- **`lib/codebases/github.ts`** — confirmed member↔login sync; stores avatar/login; derives public + **noreply** aliases. **No scan-payload changes** — identity stays out of the scanner.
- **CLI**: `add-author-alias`, `link-github`, `sync-github` (`GITHUB_TOKEN` via env only).
- Avatar column in the contributor table.

## Verification
- ✅ tsc 0 · lint clean · 75 unit · `check:docs` green (23 tables incl. `member_emails`)
- ✅ 21 data-mechanics (3 new): alias **collapse** (two identities → one mapped row w/ avatar, commits summed); alias **uniqueness** across members; **collision-safe** remap incl. already-mapped rows (no silent re-point without force)
- ✅ CLI `add-author-alias` smoke

Note: merge **after #12**. Avatars populate in prod after Phase D `link-github` (needs a PAT).

author: maty3k
body:
The big perceived-quality win for photos of people: restore faces with **GFPGAN** after upscaling. Optional, behind a `[face]` extra — the base install and GUI are unchanged.

## How it works (`upscaler/face.py`)
1. **Detect** faces with OpenCV **YuNet** (gives 5 landmarks).
2. **Align** each face to the standard FFHQ-512 template (affine from the landmarks).
3. **Restore** with **GFPGAN v1.4**, loaded via **`spandrel`** — so **no `basicsr`** (the dependency the project deliberately avoids; basicsr doesn't even install cleanly on Python 3.14).
4. **Paste back** with a feathered mask. A **Face strength** slider blends toward the original to preserve likeness.

Best-effort: an image with **no faces is returned unchanged**, and the ~349MB GFPGAN net **loads lazily** only when a face is actually found.

## Why this approach
The usual `gfpgan`/`facexlib` packages depend on `basicsr` and won't install on this env (py3.14, modern torch). spandrel (MIT) loads the GFPGAN net cleanly, and YuNet (OpenCV) provides detection+landmarks — both have py3.14 wheels. I verified the research's assumptions empirically before building.

## UI / wiring
- New **"Restore faces (GFPGAN)"** accordion on the Upscale tab (Enhance-faces checkbox + strength), wired as a post-upscale stage in `enhance()`.
- Missing extras → friendly *"install `.[face]`"* error (lazy import; GUI builds fine without them).
- `[face]` extra: `spandrel`, `spandrel_extra_arches`, `opencv-python-headless` (all pinned-hash GFPGAN/YuNet weights download at runtime).

## Verification
- End-to-end on a real face: alignment is **upright** (5px landmark residual — YuNet's order matches the template, no reorder needed), the restored face is clearly cleaner, and it blends back seamlessly (visually inspected before/after).
- `enhance(face=True)` produces `… → faces (GFPGAN) @80% …`.
- Tests: registry pinning, alignment/landmark-order, no-face passthrough (without pulling the 349MB net). **Full suite: 110 passed** (was 107).

## Licensing
GFPGAN weights are Apache-2.0; YuNet is from OpenCV Zoo. Weights download at runtime (not bundled).

author: jeanmaximiliencadic
body:
## Problem

sakura is a **public** repo, but `sast`, `security-scan`, and `test` used `runs-on: cpu` (self-hosted) for push/schedule events. The org runner group has `allows_public_repositories=false` (the safe default that avoids the public-repo self-hosted-runner RCE risk), so those runs queued forever / were cancelled and never reported a status — leaving the Actions tab perpetually un-cleared.

## Fix

Move `sast`, `security-scan`, `test` to `ubuntu-latest` for **every** event (PR runs already used `ubuntu-latest`, and the `security/pr-ci-github-hosted` branch already validated this path). Toolchains are set up in-workflow (`setup-uv`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`), so nothing depends on the self-hosted image.

`publish.yml` (release pipeline) is intentionally left on the self-hosted runner.

We did **not** enable `allows_public_repositories` (would re-introduce the audit's #1 RCE risk).

body:
## What
- Extract the pure comment-match predicate into `src/repair/comment-match.ts` (`commentMatchesExisting`) and unit-test it.
- Make `postIssueComment` idempotent: on a transient gh failure, re-check for an already-posted comment before retrying, so a lost-response POST can't double-post.
- Fix the predicate's empty-marker bug: an empty idempotency marker no longer matches every comment.
- Correct the `findExistingComment` marker param type (`LooseRecord` → `string`; it was always a string).

## Why
`postIssueComment` posted with the default 6-attempt retry. If a POST succeeded but its response was lost (gateway timeout), the retry posted a second identical comment. The marker-dedup helper existed but was not applied on the retry path. Now a transient failure re-checks (by idempotency marker, else exact body) before retrying.

## Design notes
- The pure predicate lives in its own module because `apply-result.ts` self-executes its apply pipeline at import time (no main guard), so it cannot be imported by a unit test — same pattern as #103.
- Retry trade-off: the retry now does at most 2 POST attempts (was 6), with a dedup re-check between, rather than 6 blind retries. Preserving the full 6-attempt backoff would require exporting `sleepMs` from `github-cli.ts`, which this change keeps unchanged.

## Verification
- 5 new characterization tests for `commentMatchesExisting` (including the empty-marker bug).
- `pnpm check` green; `test:repair` 420 tests, fail 0; `lint:repair` clean.

Note: this touches `apply-result.ts`, which #103 also touches (different functions — policy validators vs comment helpers). Merge #103 first; this rebases cleanly.

Plan: `plans/004-idempotent-issue-comments.md`.

author: benjsz
body:
## Summary

Two stacked refactors of the Spyre testing surface:

1. **Reusable CI workflow.** Eliminate ~970 lines of duplication between `test_pull_request.yaml` and `daily_test.yaml` by extracting their shared matrix into `_spyre_tests.yaml` (`workflow_call`).
2. **Spyre tests as pytest.** Convert the five `__main__`-driven Spyre scripts under `tests/` to pytest modules with real per-model assertions, and split the 19 generate-edge-cases into one file per case so the CI matrix gives each (model × case) pair its own runner process.

## Changes

### Reusable CI workflow

- **`_spyre_tests.yaml`** (new, `workflow_call`) — holds the matrix jobs PR and daily ran identically, plus a `spyre-generate-edge-cases-tests` job gated by `run_generate_edge_cases`. Inputs: `models_filter`, `pytest_marker`, `run_generate_edge_cases`, plus `torch_spyre_ref` / `rpm_*` passthroughs. Secrets declared explicitly for `secrets: inherit`.
- **`test_pull_request.yaml`** — invokes the reusable with PR inputs (narrow filter, `not slow`, edge-cases off). Keeps PR-only pieces: triggers, pre-commit, the `run-spyre-unit-tests` fan-in gate consumed by branch protection.
- **`daily_test.yaml`** — invokes the reusable with daily inputs (broader filter, no marker, edge-cases on). Keeps the schedule + dispatch overrides; header comment now notes the (model × case) edge-case fan-out.
- **`spyre-block-compare-tests` disabled** — the test passes but SIGABRTs on interpreter shutdown (`libtorch_python.so` destructor + senlib), reddening CI. Tracked in #62.

### Spyre tests as pytest

- **`tests/spyre/`** — new tree with its own `conftest.py` that does NOT do the CPU `DEVICE` patch, so Spyre tests bind to `DEVICE="spyre"` (the source default). Skips at collection on hosts without `torch_spyre`, and on mixed `pytest tests/` runs where the parent CPU patch already fired.
- **`tests/conftest.py`** — gains a `_running_spyre_only()` guard so the entire CPU-patching block (the `hf_adapters` package shim and the `model_registry` pre-population) is skipped when pytest targets only `tests/spyre/`.
- **`pyproject.toml`** — drops `--ignore-glob=tests/test_*spyre*.py`. Adds the `spyre_block` marker for the per-layer block compare, which CI keeps disabled until the SIGABRT is root-caused.
- **Per-model assertion thresholds pinned in each test:**
  - `test_e2e_token_compare_spyre.py`: prefill logit max-diff + greedy top-1 ratio per model (default 1.0 / 3-of-5; 0.5 / 4-of-5 for known-good families).
  - `test_e2e_embed_compare_spyre.py`: per-row min cosine ≥ 0.99 (default), per-model overrides reserved.
  - `test_block_cpu_vs_spyre.py`: per-layer max-abs-diff < 0.5 with no NaN.
  - `test_e2e_smoke_spyre.py` / `test_load_spyre.py`: each existing boolean check asserted individually.

### Edge-cases split

- **`tests/spyre/edge_cases/` — 19 files, one per case** (9 greedy regimes, 4 forced-EOS, 6 special: `zero_new_tokens`, `sampling_determinism`, `no_eos_runs_full_budget`, `no_pad_token_fallback`, `sampling_top_k_zero`, `eos_inside_prompt`). Each is parametrized over the model registry.
- **`multiprocessing.Pool` is gone** — the size-1 spawn pool that gave VFIO DMA isolation between cases is replaced by the CI matrix fanning out `(model × case_file)`. Each cell is its own runner process — same boundary at lower complexity.
- **Shared helpers** (`run_greedy_case`, `run_forced_eos_case`, `load_spyre_model`, `load_hf_reference`) live in `tests/spyre/edge_cases/_common.py`.
- **`SPYRE_CASE_KEYS` / `SPYRE_EOS_CASE_KEYS`** removed from `_generate_edge_case_helpers.py` — the curated subset is now encoded in the filesystem (which case files exist).

### Docs

- `CLAUDE.md`, `ONBOARDING.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`: pytest invocations and per-case layout references.

## Test plan

- [ ] PR CI green on this branch with every previously-PR matrix job running (block-compare absent is expected, `spyre-generate-edge-cases-tests` deselected on PR is expected).
- [ ] Manual `workflow_dispatch` of `daily_test.yaml` runs the broader filter + the new (model × case) edge-cases matrix successfully.
- [ ] `run-spyre-unit-tests` still resolves and gates merges.
- [ ] Secrets (`HF_TOKEN`, `ARTIFACTORY_*`) reach the reusable via `secrets: inherit`.
- [ ] On a Spyre pod, `pytest -s -vvv tests/spyre/test_load_spyre.py -k qwen3` passes; same for token-compare, embed-compare, smoke.
- [ ] On a CPU-only host, `pytest tests/` collects cleanly and skips everything under `tests/spyre/` for missing `torch_spyre`.

## Overview
This PR implements the machine learning data pipeline and model definition for the Signal Classifier API, completing GitHub Issue #6. It covers data loading, independent z-score normalization per channel per sample, stratified splitting (train, val, test) considering both Modulation Class and SNR, and the definition of a 3-block 1D CNN model.


## Key Changes
1. **Model Definition (`src/model.py`)**:
   - Implemented the `SignalClassifier` class using PyTorch.
   - Built a 3-block 1D CNN architecture: each block consists of `Conv1d` (filters: `64 -> 128 -> 256`, kernel size `3`), `BatchNorm1d`, `ReLU`, and `MaxPool1d`.
   - Utilized `AdaptiveAvgPool1d(1)` for Global Average Pooling to reduce parameter size and enable input sequence length flexibility.
   - Added a classification head with `Dropout(0.5)` and a `Linear` layer mapping to 11 modulation class logits.
   - Total model parameters: **~127,435** (well within the target ~250K constraint for fast CPU serving).

2. **Data Pipeline (`src/data_pipeline.py`)**:
   - Implemented `load_and_split_data` to load `RML2016.10a_dict.pkl`.
   - Applied per-sample z-score normalization on both channels independently to avoid any data leakage.
   - Added strict stratified data splitting (70% train / 15% val / 15% test) across all combinations of Modulation Class and SNR.
   - Added a custom PyTorch dataset wrapper `SignalDataset` to ease loading data into training loops.

3. **Development Dependencies (`requirements-dev.txt`)**:
   - Added `torch>=2.2.0` to development requirements (retaining CPU-only/framework-agnostic serving dependencies in production `requirements.txt`).

4. **Testing & Quality Gates**:
   - Implemented `tests/test_model.py` to verify model forward pass tensor shapes and validate output correctness (no NaNs/Infs).
   - Implemented `tests/test_data_pipeline.py` to verify normalization math, strict stratification split ratios, and `SignalDataset` functionality.
   - All 22 tests pass successfully.
   - Static analysis (`ruff check` and `mypy` strict type checking) is fully compliant.

author: kali834x
body:
### Summary

`GetProduct` parses the product id out of the commissionable-node VP TXT record value. Its guard is `if (plussign < value.size() - 1)`. When the value is empty, which is what an on-wire `VP=` entry produces (ParseTxtRecord hands such an entry over as an empty ByteSpan), `value.size()` is 0 and `value.size() - 1` wraps to SIZE_MAX, so the branch runs anyway. It then forms `value.data() + plussign + 1`, i.e. `nullptr + 1`, and sets `productStrLen = value.size() - plussign - 1`, also SIZE_MAX. The value comes straight off the wire from an unauthenticated mDNS responder during discovery, so a peer reaches this with a crafted TXT record. Rewriting the check as `plussign + 1 < value.size()` is underflow-safe and yields the same result for every valid input.

### Related issues

None.

### Testing

Added an empty-value case to `TestGetProduct`. A standalone build of the guard arithmetic under `-fsanitize=undefined,address` reports `applying non-zero offset 1 to null pointer` at the `value.data() + plussign + 1` line for an empty value; with the fix the branch is skipped and `GetProduct` returns 0.

body:
## Bug

`mathematica_code()` prints several elementary functions with their lowercase SymPy names, which is invalid Wolfram Language syntax. Wolfram Language uses capitalized function names exclusively.

Affected functions and their wrong output before this fix:

| Expression | Before (wrong) | After (correct) |
|---|---|---|
| `floor(x)` | `floor[x]` | `Floor[x]` |
| `ceiling(x)` | `ceiling[x]` | `Ceiling[x]` |
| `sign(x)` | `sign[x]` | `Sign[x]` |
| `re(x)` | `re[x]` | `Re[x]` |
| `im(x)` | `im[x]` | `Im[x]` |
| `frac(x)` | `frac[x]` | `FractionalPart[x]` |

## Root cause

The `known_functions` dict in `sympy/printing/mathematica.py` was missing entries for these functions. `_print_Function` falls back to `expr.func.__name__ + "[...]" ` which produces lowercase names, invalid in Mathematica.

## Fix

Add the six missing entries to `known_functions` and add corresponding assertions to `test_Function`.

author: atomiks
body:
Follow-up to #4964.

https://deploy-preview-5062--base-ui.netlify.app/react/components/combobox#virtualized

Documents memoizing combobox and autocomplete items as a simpler alternative to virtualization. For lists large enough to feel per-keystroke re-renders but not large enough to virtualize, wrapping each item in `React.memo` and passing the item as a prop lets unchanged options skip re-rendering — filtering preserves each item's reference, so the memo bails. Works for flat and grouped lists with no library changes.

Adds a `#### Memoizing items` subsection under **Virtualized** on both the combobox and autocomplete pages (autocomplete reuses the same `List`/`Collection` internals, so the pattern and the numbers below apply to both). Frames the two approaches as complementary: memoization helps up to roughly 1,000 items, beyond which mounting every option on open dominates and virtualization becomes necessary.

## Measured impact

Combobox, 1,000 items with rich children (an indicator + a label), typing a prefix that keeps all 1,000 mounted — the worst case for re-renders. The robust, machine-independent signal is the re-render count per keystroke:

- **Without memo:** all 1,000 item subtrees re-render on every keystroke.
- **With `React.memo`:** 0 memoized item re-renders — verified with a render-count probe, including when an ancestor re-renders each keystroke.

Wall-clock median ms/keystroke (synchronous input update work), production-minified build, Chromium with DevTools CPU throttling. Absolute numbers vary by machine; ranges span two independent setups:

| CPU throttle | Without memo | With `React.memo` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None (1×) | ~7–12 ms | ~1–5 ms |
| 20× slowdown | ~165–240 ms | ~6–17 ms |

On a 20×-throttled device that's a sixth of a second or more per keystroke (visibly janky), dropping by more than 10× into the low tens of ms.

author: ginderjeremiah
body:
## Summary

Fixes the per-skill vs. global damage-statistic divergence (#835).

`BattleSkill.Update` recorded the **raw** `CalculateDamage` result per skill *before* the hit, while `DamageTarget` booked the **actual** post-crit/post-defense/block value into the global stats. The two were sourced from different values for the same hit and could never reconcile:

- A **crit** made the per-skill total *understate* real damage (raw is pre-multiplier).
- High enemy **Defense** made it *overstate* it (raw is pre-mitigation).
- A per-entity challenge keyed to a specific skill (same `EStatisticType`, keyed by id — e.g. `DamageDealt`) was evaluated against raw, un-mitigated, non-crit damage, which is simply wrong.

## What changed

- **`BattleContext.DamageTarget`** now returns the actual damage it applies (the same value it books into `PlayerDamageDealt` / `HighestPlayerAttack`).
- **`BattleSkill.Update`** deals the hit first and feeds the returned actual damage to `RecordSkillUse`, instead of recording the raw `CalculateDamage` result up front. Recording necessarily follows the hit now, since crit/defense are computed inside `DamageTarget`. `RecordSkillUse`'s own contract is unchanged (it still records whatever value it's handed), so its existing unit tests stand.

## How it addresses the issue

Picks the **actual** post-crit/post-defense definition of "damage dealt" — matching the global stat — and records that per skill, exactly the suggested direction. Block/dodge only apply to enemy→player hits, which aren't per-skill recorded (player-only), so the per-skill-relevant clamp is the enemy's Defense on the player's outgoing hit; both that and the crit case are covered.

Stats are server-only (the frontend computes no per-skill stats), so nothing mirrors on the frontend and no parity surface is touched.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build` — clean, 0 warnings.
- [x] `dotnet test` — all backend suites green (Core 578, Application 281, Api 502, Infrastructure 37).
- [x] New `BattleSkillTests` reconciliation pair — asserts per-skill `TotalDamage`/`HighestSingleAttack` equal the global stats (and differ from the raw value) under both a **crit** (understate) and an **enemy-Defense clamp** (overstate).
- [x] `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` — clean.

Closes #835

## Summary / 摘要

实现 ROADMAP #2（whole-word 匹配）与 #15（正则搜索）的工具函数侧。把 `findSearchMatches` / `replaceAllMatches` 的 `SearchOptions` 扩展为支持 `wholeWord` 与 `regexp` 两个新选项，并对非法正则做 graceful fallback（返回空结果 / 原文档，而非抛错）。

## Motivation / 背景与动机

- Issue: N/A（开放命题面试 PR）
- Roadmap (docs/ROADMAP.md):
  - **#2 whole-word 匹配**（P1、planned），由本 PR 转为 done
  - **#15 正则搜索**（P1、in-progress；PR #9 in review）—— 本 PR 仅补完**导出工具函数**侧，与 PR #9 的搜索面板 UI / `SearchQuery` 改动**互不重叠**
- OpenSpec change: N/A —— 现有 `SearchOptions` 增量扩展，无破坏性变更

PR 之前的状态：
- `plugin-search` 暴露的 `NexusSearchPanel` 已通过 CM6 `SearchQuery` 原生支持 `wholeWord` / `regexp`（面板上的 `wholeWordField` / `regexpField` checkbox 已就位）
- 但导出的**独立工具函数** `findSearchMatches(doc, query, options)` 与 `replaceAllMatches(doc, query, replacement, options)` 只支持 `caseSensitive`，宿主在编辑器外做批量字符串处理（跨文件搜索、headless 替换脚本、测试断言）时拿不到面板已有的能力 —— 两条路径行为不对称

本 PR 把工具函数与面板能力对齐，**不引入新 API**，仅扩展现有 `SearchOptions` 接口。

## Changes / 变更内容

- `packages/plugin-search`:
  - `src/index.ts`:
    - `SearchOptions` 接口新增 `wholeWord?: boolean` 与 `regexp?: boolean`
    - 抽出 `buildSearchPattern(query, options): RegExp | null` 辅助函数，统一三种模式（普通 / wholeWord / regexp / 组合）的 RegExp 构造
    - **正则模式**：query 不再 escape，直接作为 pattern；`wholeWord + regexp` 组合时用 `\b(?:${query})\b` 包裹以避免与用户 query 内的 alternation `|` 优先级冲突
    - **非法正则 graceful fallback**：`buildSearchPattern` 内 `try { new RegExp(...) } catch { return null }`；`findSearchMatches` 返回 `[]`、`replaceAllMatches` 返回原 `doc`，避免抛错打断宿主调用链
  - 测试：新增 7 cases（详见 Testing 段）
- `packages/core`: 无改动
- 其他：无文档 / 配置改动

## Testing / 测试

- [x] `pnpm test` passes / 全绿 —— **343 / 343 通过**（合并 #1 多行列表的 13 cases 后；本 PR 单独跑 plugin-search 为 17 cases，已含 10 个原有 case）
- [x] Affected package builds (`pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-plugin-search build`) 通过
- [x] `pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-plugin-search exec tsc --noEmit` 类型检查无报错
- [x] New / updated vitest cases / 新增 vitest 用例 —— `packages/plugin-search/test/plugin-search.test.ts` 新增 **7 cases**：
  - whole-word 部分 (3)：
    - whole-word 匹配 `"cat"` 不命中 `"cats"` / `"catalog"`
    - case-sensitive + whole-word 组合 —— `"Cat"` 在 `"cat Cat CAT"` 中只命中 `Cat`
    - `replaceAllMatches` whole-word 模式只替换完整单词
  - regex 部分 (4)：
    - 基本数字模式 `\d+`
    - 多字段日期模式 `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`
    - case-sensitive regex —— `h.llo` 只命中 `hello`，不命中 `Hello` / `HELLO`
    - 非法正则 graceful fallback —— `findSearchMatches` 返回 `[]`，`replaceAllMatches` 返回原 doc
  - 组合 (1)：regex + wholeWord 同开 —— `cat|dog` 在 `"cat cats concatenate"` 中只命中独立 `cat`
- [ ] Manual UI check in electron-demo / electron-demo 手动验证 —— **未做**：面板侧 UI 由 CM6 `SearchQuery` 直接驱动，**不经过本 PR 改动的工具函数**（详见下方"边界说明"），无需 UI 验证

## Checklist / 自检清单

- [x] Title follows Conventional Commits / 标题遵循 Conventional Commits（`feat(search): ...`）
- [x] Public API changes update package README / types —— `SearchOptions` 类型已扩展并随 `dist/index.d.ts` 一并构建；`plugin-search` 未提供独立 README
- [x] Touched `live-preview-table.ts` → walked through the 12 Table Widget rules in CLAUDE.md —— **本 PR 未触及 `live-preview-table.ts`**
- [x] New capability / breaking change → OpenSpec proposal linked / 新 capability 或破坏性变更已附 OpenSpec —— N/A：现有接口增量扩展
- [x] No secrets / personal vault data committed / 无敏感信息被提交

## 边界说明（评审参考）

**本 PR 与 PR #9（in review 的 #15 正则搜索）的关系**：

- `NexusSearchPanel.commit()` 把面板字段打包成 `SearchQuery` 并 dispatch 给编辑器，**面板搜索完全走 CM6 内部引擎**，不经过 `findSearchMatches` / `replaceAllMatches`
- 因此本 PR 只动**独立工具函数**侧，与 PR #9 的面板 / `SearchQuery` 改动正交，不存在 conflict
- 两条路径合流后用户可以在面板与脚本中获得一致的搜索能力

**为什么对非法正则选择 graceful fallback 而非抛错？**

`findSearchMatches` 用于"实时联想"场景（用户每次按键都重算结果），非法正则在输入过程中是**常态**而非异常（`(` 输入到一半就是非法的）。抛错会让宿主必须包 `try/catch`，并要决定"半路非法是显示空列表还是保留上次结果" —— 把策略锁死在工具函数侧反而限制宿主选择。返回 `[]` / 原 doc 表达的语义是"当前没有命中"，宿主可以叠加"上次结果防抖"等高级行为。

## Out of scope（识别但本 PR 不做）

- **正则模式的 replace 捕获组验证**：JS `String.replace` 原生支持 `$1` / `$2` 等捕获组替换，本 PR 通过测试 `replaceAllMatches("foo bar baz", "(\\w+)", "[$1]", { regexp: true })` 隐式验证（已在 #15 范围）；但当前**未单独**加测试断言（commit message 中提及但代码未落地），建议合入后另开小 PR 补
- **面板侧的非法正则 UX 反馈**（红框、错误提示）：由 PR #9 负责面板侧，本 PR 不涉及
- **fuzzy / fzf 匹配**：Roadmap #17（P2），独立条目
- **多 query 同时搜索 / 排除模式**：超出 #2 / #15 范围

## Screenshots / Recordings · 截图或录屏 (UI changes)

N/A —— 工具函数扩展，无 UI 改动。使用示例：

```ts
import { findSearchMatches, replaceAllMatches } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search";

// 整词匹配：避开 cats / catalog
findSearchMatches("cat cats catalog", "cat", { wholeWord: true });
// → [{ from: 0, to: 3, text: "cat" }]

// 正则匹配：日期
findSearchMatches("2024-01-15 to 2024-12-31", "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}", { regexp: true });
// → [{ from: 0, to: 10, ... }, { from: 14, to: 24, ... }]

// 非法正则 → 空数组，不抛错
findSearchMatches("anything", "[invalid(", { regexp: true });
// → []
```

## R1.9 — Reel generator sprint: cutout-layer compositing in motion

Composites the athlete's **alpha cutout as a separate animated foreground plane with parallax**, giving photo-bearing motion cards real depth over the scrimmed full-bleed background photo the scenes already paint. Built exactly to the roadmap's declared region — a new auto-discovered sprint layer plus a distinct asset-prep fn in `motion.py` — with **zero edits to the shared `StoryCard.tsx` scene code** (🟡 DISTINCT-REGION, merge-safe).

### What landed
- **`sprint/layers/cutout.tsx`** — new additive overlay (auto-discovered by the sprint layer registry). Frame-pure entrance + ambient parallax: a slow Ken-Burns-style push plus horizontal drift and vertical float **orthogonal to the background's vertical drift** (that orthogonality is what reads as two separate depth planes), seed-keyed so siblings don't bob in lockstep, displacement held ≤ 24px so the cut edge never reveals background it can't show. Composition-aware placement *opposite* the scene text; left-side subjects mirror like the still. **Strict no-op when no cut is prepared**, so cards without a sourced photo render byte-identically.
- **`visual/motion.py::_cutout_data_uri_for_brief`** — the distinct asset-prep fn. Runs the **same configured background remover the still renderer uses** (`media_ai.providers.get_bg_remover`), caches the alpha PNG per source photo, then downscales + inlines it (Remotion's headless Chromium only sees what the props carry). Honest on every miss: only a *real* remover is used (never rembg's passthrough rectangle), and it returns `""` on any failure rather than failing a render. Wired into `_card_to_props` as `cutoutSrc` and recorded on the explainability manifest as `has_cutout`.
- **`StoryCard.tsx` / `Root.tsx`** — the `cutoutSrc` card-schema field (the same mechanism `photoSrc` uses to carry a prepared asset through to a layer).

### Honesty / determinism
- Pure function of the frame (Remotion `interpolate` + frame-derived sinusoids) — no `Math.random`, no wallclock; same props → byte-identical re-render.
- The cut is the same evidence the still composites — no fabricated subject, no recolour; the seating shadow uses the resolved brand `ground` role, never an invented hex.
- Prop-shape change bumps the render cache key (no stale silent renders).

body:
## Keystone: typed bound-value IR + value carrier

Implements `epic-silasx-reactive-responsive-layout-bound-value-ir` — the keystone every
other feature in the reactive/responsive-layout epic builds on. Lifts the load-time
`LayoutValueError::DynamicValue` fail-closed for layout `{expr}` by **lowering a bound
value to a typed descriptor**, without weakening the static parser, and un-spikes the
runtime value carrier to hold a §8a-canonical float.

### What's in here (3 stories)
- **carrier** — sealed `BoundNumber(u64)` newtype (private field; `from_f64`
  canonicalizes via `digest::canonical_f64_bits`, so `Eq`/`Ord` over the bits are sound:
  `-0.0 == +0.0`, all-NaN collapse) + `BoundScalar::Number`. `F64` arms at every
  `DataValue → BoundValue` seam (`project_delta_value`, `data_value_to_bound_value`);
  `U64 → i64` via `try_from` (no wrap); int-only memo (`SumInts`/`LayoutIsland`) fails
  closed on `Number`/overflow instead of contributing a silent `0`.
- **coercion-resolution** — numeric→`f32`-dimension coercion + resolution-semantics
  policy table (pending / absent / redacted / wrong-type / NaN / inf / out-of-range),
  all fail-closed per property (no §7b blanket clamp, no `last-good`, no silent-`0`).
  Integer and f64 narrowing fail closed at the exact-range boundary (incl. `i64::MAX`).
- **descriptor-lowering** — `BoundLayoutValue` / `BoundPaintValue` descriptors;
  `width: {expr}` lowers to a descriptor. Bound style reads are routed through the
  **validated read-site pipeline** (`UiBindingValidator`) so unresolved/unauthorized
  style reads fail closed at compile, and the descriptor's canonical bytes encode the
  **validated read-source identity** (`lowering().canonical_bytes()`) — not the per-tick
  value — keeping the plan digest stable across ticks.

Plan canonical-bytes schema bumped (descriptor sections); goldens re-baselined.

### Review
Designed with a dual cross-review (Codex + Opus). Post-implementation it went through a
full Codex peer-review + a separate Opus adversarial review. Findings folded: validated
read-site routing for descriptors (was a synthetic-path fail-open), `i64::MAX` saturation
fail-closed, tautological→real coercion tests, bits/decimal agreement fixture, stale
rustdoc.

Deferred to `-tier2-layout-binding` (consumer): per-tick descriptor consumption into
layout fields; conditional (`:hover`/`@media`) dynamic-dimension lowering (still
fail-closed via the static parser here); runtime capability check at consumption.

- `cargo clippy -p silas -p silas-ui-compile --all-targets`: clean (deny unsafe/missing_docs/broken-intra-doc-links holds)
